sentences.text: Terminonaris was an extinct genus of pholidosaurid crocodyliforms, a subgroup within Mesoeucrocodylia.
The skull of the largest known individual measures 109.6 cm in length.
Terminonaris is the most derived crocodile-relative known to possess scleral rings.
Its elongated snout and thin interlocking teeth suggest it hunted fish, small mammals, and possibly small dinosaurs.
Henry Fairfield Osborn described the genus in 1904, initially naming it Teleorhinus before suggesting Terminonaris as an alternative name.
Seven fossil specimens of Terminonaris have been found, six in North America and one in Europe.
The bones of Big Bert were discovered in 1991 in the Favel Formation near the Carrot River in Saskatchewan by paleontologist Tim Tokaryk with the help of local fossil hunter Dickson Hardie.
Brian Condon discovered a 96 million-year-old Terminonaris fossil in 2005 near Lake Lewisville in Texas.
Terminonaris likely stayed near the shore and only ventured into the warm, salty seaway water to hunt for fish.
Big Bert lived about 92 million years ago near the eastern shoreline of the Western Interior Seaway.
Terminonaris inhabited the Western Interior Seaway, an inland sea stretching from the Gulf of Mexico to the Arctic Ocean during the Late Cretaceous.
The oldest known Terminonaris fossil, found in Texas, lived about 96 million years ago.
The Texas fossils discovered by Brian Condon are the oldest and southernmost known examples of Terminonaris.
Terminonaris lived between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago during the Cenomanian to Turonian stages.
It is debated whether Terminonaris originated in Europe or Texas, with recent evidence suggesting a Texas origin and northward dispersal.
